tools.description: Return a fast, zero-argument health overview of the running Cruma agent. Reports an overall status (ok / degraded / critical) and a structured list of active issues across: hosted-process health (crashes, backoff, start failures), listener binding failures, config validation errors, certificate expiry or ACME failures, tunnel connectivity, and HTTP error rates from the last 10 minutes. Use this as the first call when troubleshooting — it bootstraps context before diving into specific tools.
tools.name: get_health_summary

tools.description: Return a full site card for one or more frontend hostnames, process IDs, or backend IDs. Each card includes the target entity plus all directly related entities: the listeners that serve it, the backend or process it targets (for frontends), and any frontends that reference it (for processes and backends). Use this instead of get_runtime_inventory when you want the complete picture for a specific site.

ids.description:
One or more frontend hostnames, process IDs, or backend IDs to describe.
Each entry is resolved to a site card containing the target entity and
all directly related entities (listeners, backend/process, frontends).

tools.name: get_site_summary

tools.description: Return a sanitized view of the live generated proxy listeners and HTTP routes, including route names, match filters, targets, and middleware summaries for injected routes such as cruma-local-mcp.
tools.name: get_proxy_routes

tools.description: Return the last N hosted-process log entries from the live process orchestrator, with optional case-insensitive text filtering and optional process id filtering.
tools.name: get_process_logs

tools.description: Send a LIVE route-decision probe: fire a real loopback request through the running proxy on a given listener port and return the decision the actual data plane produced. Unlike `simulate_route` (which reimplements routing offline), this exercises the real accept path and reports which plane handled it (hyper vs io_uring), fast-path eligibility, the classified request/response middleware chains, the TLS decision, and the chosen backend origin (round-robin cursor previewed, not advanced — it never dials the backend). Provide `port` (a bound HTTP-terminating listener; TLS-passthrough and raw-TCP listeners cannot answer), optionally `tls`, `sni`, `host`, `path`, `http2`. Use this to confirm ground truth when `simulate_route`'s prediction is in doubt.

inputSchema.description:
Arguments for `probe_route` — the LIVE counterpart to `simulate_route`. Where `simulate_route`
reimplements routing offline, this fires a real loopback request through the running proxy and
reports the decision the actual data plane produced (including which plane, hyper vs io_uring).

host.description:
HTTP `Host` header. Set it different from `sni` to reproduce the reused-TLS / connection
-coalescing case (a browser reusing a connection for a sibling hostname).

http2.description: Force HTTP/2 (ALPN `h2` over TLS, or prior-knowledge h2c on plaintext). Defaults to HTTP/1.1.

path.description: HTTP request path, e.g. `"/api/v1/foo"`. Defaults to `"/"`. May include a query string.

sni.description: TLS SNI to present at the handshake. Optional; defaults to `host`.

tls.description:
Whether the listener terminates TLS. Optional — if omitted, inferred from the live config's
listener on that port (defaults to plaintext when unknown).

tools.name: probe_route
